title: Staged evaluation playbook: metrics, gates, and rollback criteria for inference rollouts
creator: Laura Chen
description: Create a repeatable, documented playbook for staged inference rollouts (A/B + canary) with clear metric definitions, statistical rules, automatic gating logic, and explicit rollback criteria. This will be the canonical PM-facing guide and the checklist engineering and SRE use before any model or config deployment that could affect latency, cost, or output quality.
acceptance_criteria: A single-page playbook (this doc) approved by Product, SRE, and Applied ML owners
Stage definitions and durations (internal -> opt-in -> 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> global) documented and linked to rollout automation
Metric thresholds (quality, latency, errors, cost) expressed as absolute numbers and deltas vs baseline with rationales
Minimum exposure counts and statistical test (sequential AB or Bayesian) chosen and documented
Rollback triggers defined and wired to Console alerting and auto-fallback policies
Runbook + incident template created and linked; at least one dry-run executed in staging

metric_thresholds: Quality: pairing automated quality signals and manual spot checks. Primary signal = delta in semantic-similarity-based evals (embedding cosine) on canonical prompt-set: FAIL if median similarity decreases by >3 pts and mean decreases by >2 pts.
Hallucination: automated classifier false-positive increase >+1.5% absolute OR >25% relative -> FAIL
Latency: P95 token-latency increase >+20% absolute or >200ms -> FAIL
Errors: 5xx or inference-fallback rate >0.5% absolute OR >200% relative -> FAIL
Cost: per-token cost increases by >10% compared to pinned baseline for the route -> warn (manual review)
Adoption/Satisfaction: early feedback NPS <= -10 from internal cohort -> warn
statistical_rules: Use sequential stopped AB test (O'Brien-Fleming) for high-volume routes; require minimum 10k effective requests per variant before evaluation
For low-volume routes, use Bayesian A/B with credible intervals; require posterior probability >95% that new variant is worse for at least one primary metric to trigger rollback
Apply Bonferroni-like correction if evaluating >3 independent primary metrics to control false positives
Minimum observation window: 72h at each production stage unless failure detected earlier
Require at least two independent signals (one quality, one infra) to auto-rollback; single-signal alerts create immediate human review
decisions: Decision 2026-02-26: Use embedding-based semantic similarity as primary automated quality metric for text generation routes (applied ML agreed)
Decision 2026-02-26: P95 latency and error rate are treated as independent hard gates for auto-rollback
Decision 2026-03-01: Canary progression percentages chosen (1% -> 10% -> 50%) to balance detection speed with customer risk
Decision 2026-03-03: Opt-in internal cohort (engineers + power users) required before public canary
risks: Risk: Automated quality metrics can miss subtle hallucinations. Mitigation: mandatory manual spot-checking in each stage and a small human-in-the-loop panel for critical routes
Risk: Signal drift in baseline due to time-of-day or dataset changes. Mitigation: baseline recalibration weekly and traffic stratification by region/time
Risk: Flapping rollouts if thresholds too sensitive. Mitigation: require multiple independent signals and minimum exposure counts
Risk: Console alert fatigue. Mitigation: tiered alerts and clearly documented on-call responsibilities
auto_rollback_policy: Auto-rollback immediate conditions: any P95 latency or inference error rate breach marked as FAIL
Auto-rollback requires automated policy AND SRE approval for cost-only regressions
Fallback model variant: previous pinned model version in runtime; rollback executed via routing policy in 60s and documented in incident ticket
